es​Δy,y′​(r)=(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))s​exp⁡(s​∑m=1K∑t=1rmlog⁡(pm​(Xm,t∣y′)pm​(Xm,t∣y))).e^{s\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}=\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s}\exp\!\left(s\sum_{m=1}^{K}\sum_{t=1}^{r_{m}}\log\!\left(\frac{p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y^{\prime})}{p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y)}\right)\right).

Taking conditional expectations given Y=yY=y yields

𝔼⁡[es​Δy,y′​(r)|Y=y]=(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))s​𝔼​[exp⁡(s​∑m=1K∑t=1rmlog⁡(pm​(Xm,t∣y′)pm​(Xm,t∣y)))|Y=y].\mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{s\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\,\big|\,Y=y\right]=\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\left(s\sum_{m=1}^{K}\sum_{t=1}^{r_{m}}\log\!\left(\frac{p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y^{\prime})}{p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y)}\right)\right)\,\bigg|\,Y=y\right].

By Lemma 2, the expectation factorizes as ∏m(Mm(y,y′)​(s))rm\prod_{m}(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s))^{r_{m}}. Substituting into (17) and minimizing over s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1] proves (9). ∎

B.3 Proof of Theorem 2

Proof of Theorem 2.

Fix y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y} and r∈ℤ≥0Kr\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{K}. By Lemma 1,

Pe​(y,r)≤∑y′∈𝒴∖{y}Pr⁡(Δy,y′​(r)≥0∣Y=y).P_{e}(y;r)\leq\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}\setminus\{y\}}\Pr\!\big(\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq 0\mid Y=y\big).

Applying Proposition 1 to each term gives

Pe​(y,r)≤∑y′∈𝒴∖{y}mins∈[0,1]⁡(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))s​∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(s))rm.P_{e}(y;r)\leq\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}\setminus\{y\}}\min_{s\in[0,1]}\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s}\prod_{m=1}^{K}\left(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\right)^{r_{m}}.

This expression equals P¯e​(y,r)\overline{P}_{e}(y;r) defined in (10), completing the proof. ∎

B.4 Proof of Theorem 3

Throughout this subsection, we use the shorthand πmin:=miny⁡π⁡(y)\pi_{\min}:=\min_{y}\pi(y), πmax:=maxy⁡π⁡(y)\pi_{\max}:=\max_{y}\pi(y), cmin:=minm⁡cmc_{\min}:=\min_{m}c_{m}, and cΣ:=∑m=1Kcmc_{\Sigma}:=\sum_{m=1}^{K}c_{m}.

To prove Theorem 3, we proceed in two stages. First, we establish a pairwise tightness result showing that the Chernoff bound for each pair (y,y′)(y,y^{\prime}) matches the true pairwise comparison probability up to a factor of order 1/n1/\sqrt{n}, where nn is the effective sample size for that pair. Second, we translate this pairwise tightness into a bound on the ratio OPT¯​(α)/OPT​(α)\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)/\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha) by showing that only O⁡(log⁡log⁡(1/αmin))O(\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min})) additional rounds of queries suffice to absorb the polynomial prefactor.

B.4.1 Pairwise Chernoff tightness

We work with a strict pairwise comparison event: for y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and r∈ℤ≥0Kr\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{K}, define Ey,y′>(r):={Δy,y′(r)>0}E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r):=\{\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)>0\}. Since Δy,y′​(r)>0\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)>0 implies that y′y^{\prime} achieves a strictly larger posterior log-likelihood than yy, we have Ey,y′>(r)⊆{Y^r(X(r))≠y}E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\subseteq\{\widehat{Y}_{r}(X(r))\neq y\} and hence Pr⁡(Ey,y′>​(r)∣Y=y)≤Pe​(y,r)\Pr(E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\mid Y=y)\leq P_{e}(y;r).

For each pair (y,y′)(y,y^{\prime}) and s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1], define the pairwise Chernoff proxy

P¯y,y′​(r,s):=(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))s​∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(s))rm,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s):=\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s}\prod_{m=1}^{K}\big(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\big)^{r_{m}}, (18)

and the optimized proxy P¯y,y′​(r):=mins∈[0,1]⁡P¯y,y′​(r,s)\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r):=\min_{s\in[0,1]}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s). From Proposition 1, we have Pr⁡(Δy,y′​(r)≥0∣Y=y)≤P¯y,y′​(r)\Pr(\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq 0\mid Y=y)\leq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) for all y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and all rr.

We also define the set of informative models ℳ(y,y′):={m:pm(⋅∣y)≠pm(⋅∣y′)}\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime}):=\{m:p_{m}(\cdot\mid y)\neq p_{m}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime})\} and the effective sample size ny,y′​(r):=∑m∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)rmn_{y,y^{\prime}}(r):=\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime})}r_{m}. By the pairwise identifiability condition, ℳ⁡(y,y′)≠∅\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime})\neq\emptyset for every y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}.

The key analytical tool is an exponential change of measure that recasts tail probabilities of Δy,y′​(r)\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) under the original model as expectations under a tilted distribution.

Remark 1 (Change of measure).

For s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1], define a tilted marginal on 𝒳m\mathcal{X}_{m} by

qm(y,y′)​(x,s):=pm​(x∣y) 1−s​pm​(x∣y′)sMm(y,y′)​(s),x∈𝒳m,q_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(x;s):=\frac{p_{m}(x\mid y)^{\,1-s}\,p_{m}(x\mid y^{\prime})^{\,s}}{M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)},\qquad x\in\mathcal{X}_{m},

and the induced product measure ℚy,y′,r,s​(X⁡(r)=x⁡(r)):=∏m,tqm(y,y′)​(xm,t,s)\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}(X(r)=x(r)):=\prod_{m,t}q_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(x_{m,t};s). Since all likelihoods are strictly positive, this is a well-defined probability measure.

The following identity expresses probabilities under the original model in terms of the tilted measure ℚy,y′,r,s\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}.

Lemma 4 (Change-of-measure identity).

For any event ℰ\mathcal{E} measurable with respect to X⁡(r)X(r),

Pr(X(r)∈ℰ∣Y=y)=P¯y,y′(r;s)𝔼ℚy,y′,r,s[e−s​Δy,y′​(r) 1{X(r)∈ℰ}].\Pr\!\big(X(r)\in\mathcal{E}\mid Y=y\big)=\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}}\Big[e^{-s\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\,\mathbf{1}\{X(r)\in\mathcal{E}\}\Big].
Proof of Lemma 4.

For a fixed realization x⁡(r)x(r), the Radon–Nikodym derivative equals

Pr⁡(X⁡(r)=x⁡(r)∣Y=y)ℚy,y′,r,s​(X⁡(r)=x⁡(r))=∏m,tpm​(xm,t∣y)qm(y,y′)​(xm,t,s)=∏m,tMm(y,y′)​(s)​(pm​(xm,t∣y)pm​(xm,t∣y′))s.\frac{\Pr(X(r)=x(r)\mid Y=y)}{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}(X(r)=x(r))}=\prod_{m,t}\frac{p_{m}(x_{m,t}\mid y)}{q_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(x_{m,t};s)}=\prod_{m,t}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\,\left(\frac{p_{m}(x_{m,t}\mid y)}{p_{m}(x_{m,t}\mid y^{\prime})}\right)^{s}.

Using the definition of Δy,y′​(r)\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) in (6), the product simplifies to P¯y,y′​(r,s)​e−s​Δy,y′​(r)\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)\,e^{-s\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}. Multiplying by ℚy,y′,r,s​(X⁡(r)=x⁡(r))\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}(X(r)=x(r)) and summing over x⁡(r)∈ℰx(r)\in\mathcal{E} yields the result. ∎

To apply Lemma 4 effectively, we need the tilting parameter ss to be chosen so that Δy,y′​(r)\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) is centered under the tilted measure.

Remark 2 (Interior minimizers and centering).

Define Ψy,y′,r​(s):=log⁡P¯y,y′​(r,s)\Psi_{y,y^{\prime},r}(s):=\log\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s) for s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1]. This function is convex (as a sum of log-sum-exp functions and a linear term in ss), and its derivative satisfies Ψ′​(s)=𝔼ℚy,y′,r,s​[Δy,y′​(r)]\Psi^{\prime}(s)=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}}[\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)] for s∈(0,1)s\in(0,1).

The next lemma confirms that, for large enough effective sample sizes, such a centering minimizer exists and is bounded away from the endpoints of [0,1][0,1].

Lemma 5 (Interior minimizers).

Under the model assumptions in Section 3 and the uniform boundedness condition, there exist constants δ∈(0,1/2)\delta\in(0,1/2) and ncen∈ℕn_{\mathrm{cen}}\in\mathbb{N} such that for any y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and any rr with ny,y′​(r)≥ncenn_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{\mathrm{cen}}, every minimizer sy,y′∗​(r)s^{*}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) of Ψy,y′,r\Psi_{y,y^{\prime},r} lies in [δ,1−δ][\delta,1-\delta] and satisfies

𝔼ℚy,y′,r,sy,y′∗​(r)​[Δy,y′​(r)]=0.\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s^{*}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}}\!\big[\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\big]=0.
Proof of Lemma 5.

Define κmin:=miny≠y′,m∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)min{DKL(pm(⋅∣y)∥pm(⋅∣y′)),DKL(pm(⋅∣y′)∥pm(⋅∣y))}>0\kappa_{\min}:=\min_{y\neq y^{\prime},\,m\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime})}\min\{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_{m}(\cdot\mid y)\|p_{m}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime})),\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_{m}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime})\|p_{m}(\cdot\mid y))\}>0. At s=0s=0, we have Ψ′(0)=log(π(y′)/π(y))−∑mrmDKL(pm(⋅∣y)∥pm(⋅∣y′))≤log(1/πmin)−κminny,y′(r)\Psi^{\prime}(0)=\log(\pi(y^{\prime})/\pi(y))-\sum_{m}r_{m}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p_{m}(\cdot\mid y)\|p_{m}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime}))\leq\log(1/\pi_{\min})-\kappa_{\min}\,n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), and similarly Ψ′​(1)≥−log⁡(1/πmin)+κmin​ny,y′​(r)\Psi^{\prime}(1)\geq-\log(1/\pi_{\min})+\kappa_{\min}\,n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r). For ny,y′​(r)n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) large enough, Ψ′​(0)<0<Ψ′​(1)\Psi^{\prime}(0)<0<\Psi^{\prime}(1), so every minimizer lies in (0,1)(0,1).

Set δ:=min⁡{κmin/(4​B2), 1/4}\delta:=\min\{\kappa_{\min}/(4B^{2}),\,1/4\}. By the mean value theorem and |Ψ′′​(s)|≤B2​ny,y′​(r)|\Psi^{\prime\prime}(s)|\leq B^{2}n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), we get Ψ′​(δ)<0<Ψ′​(1−δ)\Psi^{\prime}(\delta)<0<\Psi^{\prime}(1-\delta) for ny,y′​(r)n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) large enough, so every minimizer lies in [δ,1−δ][\delta,1-\delta]. Since Ψ\Psi is differentiable and convex on the interior, any interior minimizer satisfies Ψ′​(s∗)=0\Psi^{\prime}(s^{*})=0, which is exactly the centering condition. ∎

Under the centering tilt, Δy,y′​(r)\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) has mean zero; we next establish that its variance grows linearly in the effective sample size.

Lemma 6 (Uniform variance lower bound under the tilted measure).

Let δ∈(0,1/2)\delta\in(0,1/2) be as in Lemma 5. There exists a constant vmin>0v_{\min}>0 such that for all y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}, all rr, and all s∈[δ,1−δ]s\in[\delta,1-\delta],

Varℚy,y′,r,s​(Δy,y′​(r))≥vmin​ny,y′​(r).\mathrm{Var}_{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s}}\!\big(\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\big)\geq v_{\min}\,n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r).
Proof of Lemma 6.

For each informative model m∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)m\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime}) and each s∈[δ,1−δ]s\in[\delta,1-\delta], the tilted marginal qm(y,y′)​(⋅,s)q_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(\cdot;s) has full support on 𝒳m\mathcal{X}_{m}, and the log-likelihood ratio log⁡(pm​(X∣y′)/pm​(X∣y))\log(p_{m}(X\mid y^{\prime})/p_{m}(X\mid y)) is non-constant. Its variance under qm(y,y′)​(⋅,s)q_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(\cdot;s) is therefore strictly positive. By continuity of the variance in ss and finiteness of the set of informative triples (m,y,y′)(m,y,y^{\prime}), the minimum over all such triples and all s∈[δ,1−δ]s\in[\delta,1-\delta] is attained and positive. Since Δy,y′​(r)\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) is a sum of ny,y′​(r)n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) independent terms (one per query to an informative model), the total variance is at least vmin​ny,y′​(r)v_{\min}\,n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r). ∎

With the centering property from Lemma 5 and the variance lower bound from Lemma 6 in hand, we apply the Berry–Esseen theorem to show that a non-negligible fraction of the tilted probability mass falls in a window just above zero.

Lemma 7 (Window probability under the minimizing tilt).

There exist constants H>0H>0, nwin∈ℕn_{\mathrm{win}}\in\mathbb{N}, and β>0\beta>0 such that for every y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and every rr with ny,y′​(r)≥nwinn_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{\mathrm{win}},

ℚy,y′,r,sy,y′⋆​(r)​(0<Δy,y′​(r)≤H)≥βny,y′​(r).\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\big(0<\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\leq H\big)\geq\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}}.
Proof of Lemma 7.

Write n:=ny,y′​(r)n:=n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), s⋆:=sy,y′⋆​(r)s^{\star}:=s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), ℚ:=ℚy,y′,r,s⋆\mathbb{Q}:=\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s^{\star}}, and Δ:=Δy,y′​(r)\Delta:=\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r). For each informative model m∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)m\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime}), define Zm,t:=log⁡(pm​(Xm,t∣y′)/pm​(Xm,t∣y))Z_{m,t}:=\log(p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y^{\prime})/p_{m}(X_{m,t}\mid y)) and the centered variables Um,t:=Zm,t−𝔼ℚ​[Zm,t]U_{m,t}:=Z_{m,t}-\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[Z_{m,t}]. Let S:=∑m∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)∑t=1rmUm,tS:=\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime})}\sum_{t=1}^{r_{m}}U_{m,t}. Since 𝔼ℚ​[Δ]=0\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[\Delta]=0 (Lemma 5), we have Δ=S\Delta=S. Write σ2:=Varℚ​(S)\sigma^{2}:=\mathrm{Var}_{\mathbb{Q}}(S). By the uniform boundedness condition, |Um,t|≤2​B|U_{m,t}|\leq 2B almost surely and 𝔼ℚ​[|Um,t|3]≤(2​B)3\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}}[|U_{m,t}|^{3}]\leq(2B)^{3}. Moreover, vmin​n≤σ2≤B2​nv_{\min}\,n\leq\sigma^{2}\leq B^{2}n.

By the Berry–Esseen theorem for independent random variables, |ℚ⁡(S/σ≤z)−Φ⁡(z)|≤C0/n|\mathbb{Q}(S/\sigma\leq z)-\Phi(z)|\leq C_{0}/\sqrt{n} where C0:=CBE​(2​B)3/vmin3/2C_{0}:=C_{\mathrm{BE}}(2B)^{3}/v_{\min}^{3/2} and Φ\Phi is the standard normal cdf.

Choose H:=max⁡{1, 4​C0​B/φ⁡(1)}H:=\max\{1,\,4C_{0}B/\varphi(1)\} and nwin:=max⁡{ncen,⌈H2/vmin⌉}n_{\mathrm{win}}:=\max\{n_{\mathrm{cen}},\,\lceil H^{2}/v_{\min}\rceil\}, where φ(z):=(2π)−1/2e−z2/2\varphi(z):=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-z^{2}/2}. For n≥nwinn\geq n_{\mathrm{win}}, we have σ≥H\sigma\geq H and thus H/σ≤1H/\sigma\leq 1, so

Φ⁡(H/σ)−Φ⁡(0)=∫0H/σφ⁡(u)​𝑑u≥Hσ​φ​(1)≥H​φ​(1)B​n.\Phi(H/\sigma)-\Phi(0)=\int_{0}^{H/\sigma}\varphi(u)\,du\geq\frac{H}{\sigma}\,\varphi(1)\geq\frac{H\,\varphi(1)}{B\sqrt{n}}.

Therefore ℚ⁡(0<Δ≤H)≥(H​φ​(1)/B−2​C0)/n≥2​C0/n\mathbb{Q}(0<\Delta\leq H)\geq(H\varphi(1)/B-2C_{0})/\sqrt{n}\geq 2C_{0}/\sqrt{n} by the choice of HH. ∎

Combining the change-of-measure identity with the window probability estimate yields the main pairwise result.

Lemma 8 (Pairwise Chernoff tightness).

Under the model assumptions in Section 3 and the uniform boundedness condition, there exist constants n0∈ℕn_{0}\in\mathbb{N} and γ>0\gamma>0 such that for every y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and every rr with ny,y′​(r)≥n0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{0},

Pr⁡(Ey,y′>​(r)∣Y=y)≥γny,y′​(r)​P¯y,y′​(r).\Pr\!\big(E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\mid Y=y\big)\geq\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}}\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r). (19)

Together with Proposition 1, this shows that the pairwise Chernoff bound is tight up to a factor of order 1/ny,y′​(r)1/\sqrt{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}.

Proof of Lemma 8.

Set n0:=nwinn_{0}:=n_{\mathrm{win}} and fix y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and rr with n:=ny,y′​(r)≥n0n:=n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{0}. Let s⋆:=sy,y′⋆​(r)s^{\star}:=s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r). Applying Lemma 4 with ℰ=Ey,y′>​(r)\mathcal{E}=E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) gives

Pr⁡(Ey,y′>​(r)∣Y=y)=P¯y,y′​(r,s⋆)​𝔼ℚy,y′,r,s⋆​[e−s⋆​Δy,y′​(r)​ 1​{Ey,y′>​(r)}].\Pr\!\big(E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\mid Y=y\big)=\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s^{\star})\,\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{Q}_{y,y^{\prime},r,s^{\star}}}\Big[e^{-s^{\star}\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\,\mathbf{1}\{E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\}\Big].

On {0<Δy,y′(r)≤H}⊆Ey,y′>(r)\{0<\Delta_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\leq H\}\subseteq E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), we have e−s⋆​Δ≥e−He^{-s^{\star}\Delta}\geq e^{-H} since s⋆∈[0,1]s^{\star}\in[0,1]. Substituting P¯y,y′​(r,s⋆)=P¯y,y′​(r)\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s^{\star})=\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r) and applying Lemma 7, we obtain

Pr⁡(Ey,y′>​(r)∣Y=y)≥P¯y,y′​(r)​e−H​βn.\Pr\!\big(E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\mid Y=y\big)\geq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\,e^{-H}\,\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{n}}.

Thus (19) holds with γ:=β​e−H\gamma:=\beta e^{-H}. ∎

B.4.2 From pairwise tightness to the cost ratio bound

For n∈ℤ≥0n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}, define the nn-round augmentation r+n:=r+n​𝟏r^{+n}:=r+n\mathbf{1} where 𝟏=(1,…,1)∈ℤ≥0K\mathbf{1}=(1,\ldots,1)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{K}. The following lemma shows that each additional round contracts the pairwise Chernoff proxy by a fixed factor.

Lemma 9 (Geometric contraction).

Let δ\delta be as in Lemma 5 and define

ϑ:=max⁡∏m=1Ky≠y′s∈[δ,1−δ]⁡Mm(y,y′)​(s).\vartheta:=\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}y\neq y^{\prime}\\ s\in[\delta,1-\delta]\end{subarray}}\prod_{m=1}^{K}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s).

Then ϑ∈(0,1)\vartheta\in(0,1). Moreover, for any y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}, any rr, any n≥0n\geq 0, and any s∈[δ,1−δ]s\in[\delta,1-\delta],

P¯y,y′​(r+n,s)≤ϑn​P¯y,y′​(r,s).\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{+n};s)\leq\vartheta^{n}\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s). (20)
Proof of Lemma 9.

For s∈(δ,1−δ)⊂(0,1)s\in(\delta,1-\delta)\subset(0,1) and any pair y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}, Hölder’s inequality gives Mm(y,y′)​(s)≤1M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\leq 1 with equality only if pm(⋅∣y)=pm(⋅∣y′)p_{m}(\cdot\mid y)=p_{m}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime}). Since at least one model distinguishes every pair, ∏mMm(y,y′)​(s)<1\prod_{m}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)<1. By continuity and compactness, the maximum ϑ\vartheta over all pairs and all s∈[δ,1−δ]s\in[\delta,1-\delta] is attained and lies in (0,1)(0,1). The inequality (20) follows from P¯y,y′​(r+n,s)=P¯y,y′​(r,s)​∏mMm(y,y′)​(s)n≤P¯y,y′​(r,s)​ϑn\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{+n};s)=\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)\prod_{m}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)^{n}\leq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)\,\vartheta^{n}. ∎

The pairwise tightness bound in Lemma 8 requires ny,y′​(r)≥n0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{0}. The next lemma shows that, for sufficiently small tolerances, any robustly feasible design automatically satisfies this condition.

Lemma 10 (Small tolerances force large effective sample sizes).

Define ηmin:=minm,y,x⁡pm​(x∣y)>0\eta_{\min}:=\min_{m,y,x}p_{m}(x\mid y)>0 and ε0:=ηminn0−1\varepsilon_{0}:=\eta_{\min}^{\,n_{0}-1}, where n0n_{0} is as in Lemma 8. For every pair y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and every rr with ny,y′​(r)≤n0−1n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\leq n_{0}-1,

max⁡{Pe​(y,r),Pe​(y′,r)}≥ε0.\max\big\{P_{e}(y;r),\,P_{e}(y^{\prime};r)\big\}\geq\varepsilon_{0}.

Consequently, if αmin<ε0\alpha_{\min}<\varepsilon_{0} and r∈ℛ⁡(α)r\in\mathcal{R}(\alpha), then ny,y′​(r)≥n0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{0} for all y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}.

Proof of Lemma 10.

If ny,y′​(r)=0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)=0, no informative model is queried, so the score difference Sy′−Sy=log⁡(π⁡(y′)/π⁡(y))S_{y^{\prime}}-S_{y}=\log(\pi(y^{\prime})/\pi(y)) is deterministic. This forces one of the two labels to be always misclassified, giving max⁡{Pe​(y,r),Pe​(y′,r)}=1≥ε0\max\{P_{e}(y;r),P_{e}(y^{\prime};r)\}=1\geq\varepsilon_{0}.

If 1≤ny,y′​(r)≤n0−11\leq n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\leq n_{0}-1, there exists an informative model m⋆∈ℳ⁡(y,y′)m^{\star}\in\mathcal{M}(y,y^{\prime}) with rm⋆≥1r_{m^{\star}}\geq 1. Because pm⋆(⋅∣y)≠pm⋆(⋅∣y′)p_{m^{\star}}(\cdot\mid y)\neq p_{m^{\star}}(\cdot\mid y^{\prime}), there exist symbols x+,x−∈𝒳m⋆x^{+},x^{-}\in\mathcal{X}_{m^{\star}} such that hm⋆​(x+)>0h_{m^{\star}}(x^{+})>0 and hm⋆​(x−)<0h_{m^{\star}}(x^{-})<0, where hm⋆​(x):=log⁡(pm⋆​(x∣y′)/pm⋆​(x∣y))h_{m^{\star}}(x):=\log(p_{m^{\star}}(x\mid y^{\prime})/p_{m^{\star}}(x\mid y)). Construct two observation patterns that agree everywhere except at (m⋆,1)(m^{\star},1): one using x+x^{+} and the other using x−x^{-}. The score differences under these patterns satisfy v+−v−=hm⋆​(x+)−hm⋆​(x−)>0v_{+}-v_{-}=h_{m^{\star}}(x^{+})-h_{m^{\star}}(x^{-})>0, so at least one of v+>0v_{+}>0 or v−<0v_{-}<0 holds. In the first case, the pattern with x+x^{+} leads to Y^r≠y\widehat{Y}_{r}\neq y and has conditional probability at least ηminny,y′​(r)≥ε0\eta_{\min}^{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\geq\varepsilon_{0} under Y=yY=y. In the second case, the pattern with x−x^{-} leads to Y^r≠y′\widehat{Y}_{r}\neq y^{\prime} with probability at least ε0\varepsilon_{0} under Y=y′Y=y^{\prime}. ∎

Combining the pairwise tightness lower bound with the minimum sample-size guarantee yields a bound on the surrogate slack.

Lemma 11 (Surrogate slack for true-feasible plans).

Fix α\alpha with αmin<ε0\alpha_{\min}<\varepsilon_{0} and let r∈ℛ⁡(α)r\in\mathcal{R}(\alpha). Then for every y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y},

P¯e​(y,r)≤L−1γ​αy​∑m=1Krm.\overline{P}_{e}(y;r)\leq\frac{L-1}{\gamma}\,\alpha_{y}\,\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{K}r_{m}}. (21)
Proof of Lemma 11.

Fix y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y. Since αmin<ε0\alpha_{\min}<\varepsilon_{0}, Lemma 10 gives ny,y′​(r)≥n0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq n_{0}. By Lemma 8, αy≥Pe​(y,r)≥Pr⁡(Ey,y′>​(r)∣Y=y)≥(γ/ny,y′​(r))​P¯y,y′​(r)\alpha_{y}\geq P_{e}(y;r)\geq\Pr(E^{>}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\mid Y=y)\geq(\gamma/\sqrt{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)})\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r), so P¯y,y′​(r)≤(αy/γ)​ny,y′​(r)≤(αy/γ)​∑mrm\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\leq(\alpha_{y}/\gamma)\sqrt{n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)}\leq(\alpha_{y}/\gamma)\sqrt{\sum_{m}r_{m}}. Summing over y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y yields (21). ∎

We now assemble the preceding lemmas to bound the additive gap between the surrogate and true optimal costs.

Proposition 3 (Additive optimality gap).

There exist constants αmin∈(0,1)\alpha_{\min}\in(0,1) and K0>0K_{0}>0 such that for sufficiently small αmin\alpha_{\min} and OPT⁡(α)<∞\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)<\infty,

0≤OPT¯​(α)−OPT⁡(α)≤K0​log⁡log⁡(1αmin).0\leq\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)-\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)\leq K_{0}\,\log\log\!\left(\frac{1}{\alpha_{\min}}\right).
Proof of Proposition 3.

Let r⋆r^{\star} be an optimal solution of the true problem with C⁡(r⋆)=OPT⁡(α)C(r^{\star})=\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha) and write N⋆:=∑mrm⋆N^{\star}:=\sum_{m}r_{m}^{\star}. We begin by bounding N⋆N^{\star} from above. Under pairwise identifiability, ρ:=maxy≠y′⁡min⁡∏ms∈[0,1]⁡Mm(y,y′)​(s)∈(0,1)\rho:=\max_{y\neq y^{\prime}}\min_{s\in[0,1]}\prod_{m}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\in(0,1). The uniform design runif​(n):=(n,…,n)r^{\mathrm{unif}}(n):=(n,\ldots,n) satisfies P¯e​(y,runif​(n))≤(L−1)​(πmax/πmin)​ρn\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\mathrm{unif}}(n))\leq(L-1)(\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min})\rho^{n}, so choosing n=O⁡(log⁡(1/αmin))n=O(\log(1/\alpha_{\min})) makes runif​(n)r^{\mathrm{unif}}(n) feasible. Although r⋆r^{\star} is feasible for the true problem, it need not be surrogate-feasible. Lemma 11 quantifies the gap: P¯e​(y,r⋆)≤(L−1)​αy​N⋆/γ\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star})\leq(L-1)\alpha_{y}\sqrt{N^{\star}}/\gamma for every yy. To close this gap, consider the padded design r⋆+n=r⋆+n𝟏r^{\star}{}^{+n}=r^{\star}+n\mathbf{1} for n∈ℤ≥0n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}. For each pair (y,y′)(y,y^{\prime}), the minimizer sy,y′⋆​(r⋆)∈[δ,1−δ]s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\in[\delta,1-\delta] by Lemma 5. Since P¯y,y′(r⋆)+n≤P¯y,y′(r⋆;+nsy,y′⋆(r⋆))\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}{}^{+n})\leq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}{}^{+n};s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})) and Lemma 9 gives P¯y,y′(r⋆;+nsy,y′⋆(r⋆))≤ϑnP¯y,y′(r⋆)\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}{}^{+n};s^{\star}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}))\leq\vartheta^{n}\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}), summing over y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y yields P¯e(y;r⋆)+n≤ϑnP¯e(y;r⋆)\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star}{}^{+n})\leq\vartheta^{n}\,\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star}). Choosing n:=⌈log⁡((L−1)​N⋆/γ)/(−log⁡ϑ)⌉n:=\lceil\log((L-1)\sqrt{N^{\star}}/\gamma)/(-\log\vartheta)\rceil therefore ensures P¯e(y;r⋆)+n≤αy\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star}{}^{+n})\leq\alpha_{y} for all yy, so r⋆∈+nℛ¯(α)r^{\star}{}^{+n}\in\overline{\mathcal{R}}(\alpha) and OPT¯​(α)≤OPT⁡(α)+n​cΣ\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)\leq\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)+n\,c_{\Sigma}.

It remains to observe that n=O⁡(log⁡log⁡(1/αmin))n=O(\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min})). We are now ready to prove Theorem 3. For the reader’s convenience, we restate it here.

Theorem 3 (Optimization-level tightness). Suppose the uniform boundedness condition is satisfied. Then for all sufficiently small αmin:=miny∈𝒴⁡αy\alpha_{\min}:=\min_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\alpha_{y}, if OPT⁡(α)<∞\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)<\infty,

1≤OPT¯​(α)OPT⁡(α)≤1+O⁡(log⁡log⁡(1/αmin)log⁡(1/αmin)).1\leq\frac{\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)}{\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)}\leq 1+O\!\left(\frac{\log\log\!\left(1/\alpha_{\min}\right)}{\log\!\left(1/\alpha_{\min}\right)}\right).

In particular, this ratio approaches 11 as αmin↓0\alpha_{\min}\downarrow 0.

Proof of Theorem 3.

The lower bound 1≤OPT¯​(α)/OPT​(α)1\leq\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)/\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha) follows from the inclusion ℛ¯​(α)⊆ℛ​(α)\overline{\mathcal{R}}(\alpha)\subseteq\mathcal{R}(\alpha). For the upper bound, Proposition 3 gives OPT¯​(α)≤OPT⁡(α)+K0​log⁡log⁡(1/αmin)\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)\leq\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)+K_{0}\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min}). It remains to show OPT⁡(α)≥Klow​log⁡(1/αmin)\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)\geq K_{\mathrm{low}}\log(1/\alpha_{\min}) for some constant Klow>0K_{\mathrm{low}}>0.

Let r⋆r^{\star} be an optimal true-feasible design with C⁡(r⋆)=OPT⁡(α)C(r^{\star})=\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha) and write N⋆:=∑mrm⋆N^{\star}:=\sum_{m}r_{m}^{\star}. Fix y⋆∈arg⁡miny⁡αyy^{\star}\in\arg\min_{y}\alpha_{y} and any competitor y′≠y⋆y^{\prime}\neq y^{\star}. By feasibility and Lemma 8, αmin≥Pr⁡(Ey⋆,y′>​(r⋆)∣Y=y⋆)≥(γ/N⋆)​P¯y⋆,y′​(r⋆)\alpha_{\min}\geq\Pr(E^{>}_{y^{\star},y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\mid Y=y^{\star})\geq(\gamma/\sqrt{N^{\star}})\,\overline{P}_{y^{\star},y^{\prime}}(r^{\star}), hence

P¯y⋆,y′​(r⋆)≤αminγ​OPT⁡(α)cmin.\overline{P}_{y^{\star},y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\leq\frac{\alpha_{\min}}{\gamma}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)}{c_{\min}}}. (22)

Define wmax:=maxm,y≠y′,s∈[0,1]⁡(−log⁡Mm(y,y′)​(s))<∞w_{\max}:=\max_{m,\,y\neq y^{\prime},\,s\in[0,1]}(-\log M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s))<\infty. Then −log⁡P¯y⋆,y′​(r⋆)≤log⁡(πmax/πmin)+(wmax/cmin)​OPT​(α)-\log\overline{P}_{y^{\star},y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\leq\log(\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min})+(w_{\max}/c_{\min})\,\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha), so

P¯y⋆,y′​(r⋆)≥exp⁡(−log⁡(πmax/πmin)−(wmax/cmin)​OPT​(α)).\overline{P}_{y^{\star},y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\geq\exp\!\big(-\log(\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min})-(w_{\max}/c_{\min})\,\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)\big). (23)

Combining (22) and (23) and taking logarithms yields

wmaxcmin​OPT​(α)≥log⁡(1αmin)−12​log⁡(OPT⁡(α)cmin)−log⁡(πmaxπmin)−log⁡(1γ).\frac{w_{\max}}{c_{\min}}\,\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)\geq\log\!\left(\frac{1}{\alpha_{\min}}\right)-\tfrac{1}{2}\log\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)}{c_{\min}}\right)-\log\!\left(\frac{\pi_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}}\right)-\log\!\left(\frac{1}{\gamma}\right).

Since OPT⁡(α)=O⁡(log⁡(1/αmin))\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)=O(\log(1/\alpha_{\min})), the right-hand side is log⁡(1/αmin)−O⁡(log⁡log⁡(1/αmin))\log(1/\alpha_{\min})-O(\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min})). For αmin\alpha_{\min} small enough, OPT⁡(α)≥Klow​log⁡(1/αmin)\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)\geq K_{\mathrm{low}}\log(1/\alpha_{\min}). Dividing the additive gap by this lower bound gives

OPT¯​(α)OPT⁡(α)≤1+K0​log⁡log⁡(1/αmin)Klow​log⁡(1/αmin),\frac{\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)}{\mathrm{OPT}(\alpha)}\leq 1+\frac{K_{0}\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min})}{K_{\mathrm{low}}\log(1/\alpha_{\min})},

which is 1+O⁡(log⁡log⁡(1/αmin)/log⁡(1/αmin))1+O(\log\log(1/\alpha_{\min})/\log(1/\alpha_{\min})) as αmin→0\alpha_{\min}\to 0, yielding the stated bound in Theorem 3. ∎

B.5 Proof of Theorem 4

This subsection proves the AFPTAS guarantee stated in Theorem 4. We first collect the supporting lemmas that the proof requires. Throughout, we use the shorthand αmin:=miny⁡αy\alpha_{\min}:=\min_{y}\alpha_{y}, πmin:=miny⁡π⁡(y)\pi_{\min}:=\min_{y}\pi(y), πmax:=maxy⁡π⁡(y)\pi_{\max}:=\max_{y}\pi(y), cmin:=minm⁡cmc_{\min}:=\min_{m}c_{m}, cΣ:=∑m=1Kcmc_{\Sigma}:=\sum_{m=1}^{K}c_{m}, and 𝒫:={(y,y′)∈𝒴2:y≠y′}\mathcal{P}:=\{(y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{Y}^{2}:y\neq y^{\prime}\}.

B.5.1 Supporting lemmas

The first lemma provides a feasibility condition and an upper bound on the total number of queries in any optimal surrogate design.

Lemma 12 (Crude feasible design and query-count bound).

Define the pairwise contraction ρ:=maxy≠y′⁡min⁡∏m=1Ks∈[0,1]⁡Mm(y,y′)​(s)\rho:=\max_{y\neq y^{\prime}}\min_{s\in[0,1]}\prod_{m=1}^{K}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s). n≥nunif:=⌈log⁡((L−1)​πmaxπmin​αmin)−log⁡ρ⌉.n\;\geq\;n_{\mathrm{unif}}:=\left\lceil\frac{\log\!\Big(\frac{(L-1)\,\pi_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}\,\alpha_{\min}}\Big)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil. (24)

N⁡(r⋆):=∑m=1Krm⋆≤nunif​cΣcmin+kmax​K=:Nmax.N(r^{\star}):=\sum_{m=1}^{K}r_{m}^{\star}\;\leq\;\frac{n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma}}{c_{\min}}+k_{\max}\,K\;=:\;N_{\max}. (25)

For any y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime} and r=runif​(n)r=r^{\mathrm{unif}}(n),

P¯y,y′​(r)=mins∈[0,1]⁡(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))s​∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(s))n≤πmaxπmin​ρn.\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)=\min_{s\in[0,1]}\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s}\prod_{m=1}^{K}\left(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\right)^{n}\leq\frac{\pi_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}}\,\rho^{n}.

Summing over y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y gives P¯e​(y,r)≤(L−1)​(πmax/πmin)​ρn\overline{P}_{e}(y;r)\leq(L-1)(\pi_{\max}/\pi_{\min})\rho^{n}. For the query-count bound, if r⋆r^{\star} is optimal then C⁡(r⋆)≤nunif​cΣC(r^{\star})\leq n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma} and N⁡(r⋆)≤C⁡(r⋆)/cmin≤nunif​cΣ/cminN(r^{\star})\leq C(r^{\star})/c_{\min}\leq n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma}/c_{\min}. Adding the term kmax​Kk_{\max}K accounts for the augmentation used in the proof of Theorem 4. ∎

The next lemma shows that the pairwise Chernoff bound is Lipschitz in the tilting parameter ss, with a Lipschitz constant controlled by the query-count bound NmaxN_{\max}.

Lemma 13 (Lipschitz bound in ss).

For any ordered pair p=(y,y′)p=(y,y^{\prime}), any s,s′∈[0,1]s,s^{\prime}\in[0,1], and any rr with N⁡(r)≤NmaxN(r)\leq N_{\max},

P¯y,y′​(r,s′)≤exp⁡(Λ​|s−s′|)​P¯y,y′​(r,s),Λ:=log⁡(πmaxπmin)+B​Nmax.\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s^{\prime})\leq\exp\!\Big(\Lambda\,|s-s^{\prime}|\Big)\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s),\qquad\Lambda:=\log\!\Big(\frac{\pi_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}}\Big)+B\,N_{\max}. (26)

We have log⁡P¯y,y′​(r,s)=s​log⁡(π⁡(y′)/π⁡(y))+∑m=1Krm​log​Mm(y,y′)​(s)\log\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)=s\log(\pi(y^{\prime})/\pi(y))+\sum_{m=1}^{K}r_{m}\log M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s). Combining and using ∑mrm=N⁡(r)≤Nmax\sum_{m}r_{m}=N(r)\leq N_{\max} gives |log⁡P¯y,y′​(r,s)−log⁡P¯y,y′​(r,s′)|≤Λ​|s−s′||\log\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s)-\log\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r;s^{\prime})|\leq\Lambda|s-s^{\prime}|, which implies (26). ∎

The next lemma establishes the DP recursion that Algorithm 4.3 uses to solve each fixed-ss subproblem. P^e​(y,t,s):=∑y′≠yA(y,y′)​(s(y,y′))​exp⁡(−Δ​t(y,y′)),y∈𝒴.\widehat{P}_{e}(y;t;s):=\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}A_{(y,y^{\prime})}\!\big(s_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big)\,\exp\!\big(-\Delta\,t_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big),\qquad y\in\mathcal{Y}. (27)
Lemma 15 (DP recursion).

Define the DP value function

DP[t]:=min{C(r):r∈ℤ≥0K,W~p(r;s)≥tp∀p∈𝒫},\mathrm{DP}[t]:=\min\Big\{C(r):r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{K},\ \widetilde{W}_{p}(r;s)\geq t_{p}\ \ \forall p\in\mathcal{P}\Big\},

with the convention DP⁡[t]=+∞\mathrm{DP}[t]=+\infty if the set is empty. Then DP⁡[𝟎]=0\mathrm{DP}[\mathbf{0}]=0, and for t≠𝟎t\neq\mathbf{0},

Proof of Lemma 15.

If t=𝟎t=\mathbf{0}, then r=𝟎r=\mathbf{0} is feasible with cost 00, so DP⁡[𝟎]=0\mathrm{DP}[\mathbf{0}]=0. Now let t≠𝟎t\neq\mathbf{0} and suppose DP⁡[t]<+∞\mathrm{DP}[t]<+\infty. Let rr be an optimizer for DP⁡[t]\mathrm{DP}[t]. Since t≠𝟎t\neq\mathbf{0}, we must have r≠𝟎r\neq\mathbf{0}, so there exists mm with rm≥1r_{m}\geq 1. Setting r′:=r−emr^{\prime}:=r-e_{m} gives C⁡(r′)=C⁡(r)−cmC(r^{\prime})=C(r)-c_{m} and W~p​(r′,s)=W~p​(r,s)−w~m,p​(s)≥(t−w~m)+,p\widetilde{W}_{p}(r^{\prime};s)=\widetilde{W}_{p}(r;s)-\widetilde{w}_{m,p}(s)\geq(t-\widetilde{w}_{m})_{+,p} for all pp. Therefore r′r^{\prime} is feasible for DP⁡[(t−w~m)+]\mathrm{DP}[(t-\widetilde{w}_{m})_{+}], giving C⁡(r)≥cm+DP⁡[(t−w~m)+]C(r)\geq c_{m}+\mathrm{DP}[(t-\widetilde{w}_{m})_{+}]. Minimizing over mm proves the “≥\geq” direction.

For the reverse direction, fix any mm with DP⁡[(t−w~m)+]<+∞\mathrm{DP}[(t-\widetilde{w}_{m})_{+}]<+\infty and let r′r^{\prime} be an optimizer for that subproblem. Setting r:=r′+emr:=r^{\prime}+e_{m} gives W~p​(r,s)=W~p​(r′,s)+w~m,p​(s)≥tp\widetilde{W}_{p}(r;s)=\widetilde{W}_{p}(r^{\prime};s)+\widetilde{w}_{m,p}(s)\geq t_{p} for all pp, so rr is feasible for DP⁡[t]\mathrm{DP}[t] with cost cm+DP⁡[(t−w~m)+]c_{m}+\mathrm{DP}[(t-\widetilde{w}_{m})_{+}]. Taking the minimum over mm yields the “≤\leq” direction. ∎

The following proposition connects the DP output to surrogate-feasibility.

Proposition 4 (Fixed-ss DP feasibility).

Fix s∈[0,1]|𝒫|s\in[0,1]^{|\mathcal{P}|}. Let t†t^{\dagger} be any minimizer of DP⁡[t]\mathrm{DP}[t] over the states t∈{0,…,Tmax}|𝒫|t\in\{0,\ldots,T_{\max}\}^{|\mathcal{P}|} satisfying P^e​(y,t,s)≤αy\widehat{P}_{e}(y;t;s)\leq\alpha_{y} for all y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y}. Let r†r^{\dagger} be the design recovered from the backpointers at t†t^{\dagger}. Then r†r^{\dagger} is surrogate-feasible for the original problem (5).

Moreover, if some design r′r^{\prime} with N⁡(r′)≤NmaxN(r^{\prime})\leq N_{\max} satisfies P^e​(y,W~​(r′,s),s)≤αy\widehat{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{W}(r^{\prime};\,s);s)\leq\alpha_{y} for all yy, then DP⁡[W~​(r′,s)]≤C⁡(r′)\mathrm{DP}[\widetilde{W}(r^{\prime};s)]\leq C(r^{\prime}) and consequently C⁡(r†)≤C⁡(r′)C(r^{\dagger})\leq C(r^{\prime}).

Proof of Proposition 4.

By Lemma 15, the recovered design r†r^{\dagger} satisfies W~p​(r†,s)≥tp†\widetilde{W}_{p}(r^{\dagger};s)\geq t^{\dagger}_{p} for all pp. Lemma 14 then gives Wp​(r†,s)≥Δ​tp†W_{p}(r^{\dagger};s)\geq\Delta\,t^{\dagger}_{p}, so

=P^e​(y,t†,s)≤αy.\displaystyle=\widehat{P}_{e}(y;t^{\dagger};s)\leq\alpha_{y}.

Surrogate-feasibility of r†r^{\dagger} for the original problem (5) then follows from Proposition 2, since feasibility for any fixed ss implies P¯e​(y,r†)≤P¯e​(y,r†,s)≤αy\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\dagger})\leq\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\dagger};s)\leq\alpha_{y} for all yy.

For the cost comparison, the design r′r^{\prime} is feasible for DP​[W~​(r′,s)]\mathrm{DP}[\widetilde{W}(r^{\prime};s)] by definition, so DP⁡[W~​(r′,s)]≤C⁡(r′)\mathrm{DP}[\widetilde{W}(r^{\prime};s)]\leq C(r^{\prime}). The final supporting lemma provides a universal lower bound on the optimal surrogate cost.

Lemma 16 (Cost lower bound).

Any surrogate-feasible design r∈ℛ¯​(α)r\in\overline{\mathcal{R}}(\alpha) satisfies

C⁡(r)≥cminB​log⁡((L−1)​πminπmax​αmin)whenever ​αmin<(L−1)​πminπmax.C(r)\;\geq\;\frac{c_{\min}}{B}\,\log\!\Big(\frac{(L-1)\,\pi_{\min}}{\pi_{\max}\,\alpha_{\min}}\Big)\qquad\text{whenever }\ \alpha_{\min}<\frac{(L-1)\,\pi_{\min}}{\pi_{\max}}. (29)
Proof of Lemma 16.

For any pair (y,y′)(y,y^{\prime}) and any s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1], Mm(y,y′)​(s)≥e−BM_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)\geq e^{-B} by the uniform boundedness condition, so ∏mMm(y,y′)​(s)rm≥e−B​N​(r)\prod_{m}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s)^{r_{m}}\geq e^{-BN(r)}. Also, (π⁡(y′)/π⁡(y))s≥πmin/πmax(\pi(y^{\prime})/\pi(y))^{s}\geq\pi_{\min}/\pi_{\max} for s∈[0,1]s\in[0,1]. Therefore P¯y,y′​(r)≥(πmin/πmax)​e−B​N​(r)\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r)\geq(\pi_{\min}/\pi_{\max})\,e^{-B\,N(r)}. Rearranging yields N⁡(r)≥1B​log⁡((L−1)​πmin/(πmax​αmin))N(r)\geq\frac{1}{B}\log((L-1)\pi_{\min}/(\pi_{\max}\alpha_{\min})), and C⁡(r)≥cmin​N​(r)C(r)\geq c_{\min}\,N(r). ∎

B.5.2 Proof of Theorem 4

For the reader’s convenience, we restate the theorem.

Theorem 4 (AFPTAS guarantee). The design r^\widehat{r} returned by Algorithm 4.3 is surrogate-feasible, and for sufficiently small αmin\alpha_{\min}, the multiplicative guarantee C⁡(r^)≤(1+ε)​OPT¯​(α)C(\widehat{r})\leq(1+\varepsilon)\,\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha) holds. The runtime is polynomial in KK, log⁡(1/αmin)\log(1/\alpha_{\min}), and 1/ε1/\varepsilon for fixed LL.

Proof of Theorem 4.

Surrogate-feasibility. Every candidate design r†​(s)r^{\dagger}(s) returned by the fixed-ss DP subroutine satisfies P¯e​(y,r†​(s),s)≤αy\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\dagger}(s);s)\leq\alpha_{y} for all y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y} by Proposition 4. Proposition 2 then implies P¯e​(y,r†​(s))≤P¯e​(y,r†​(s),s)≤αy\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\dagger}(s))\leq\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\dagger}(s);s)\leq\alpha_{y} for all yy, so each candidate is surrogate-feasible. Since r^\widehat{r} is the cheapest among all candidates, it is surrogate-feasible as well.

Runtime. The DP at each grid point has (Tmax+1)|𝒫|(T_{\max}+1)^{|\mathcal{P}|} states, and each recursion step in (28) requires O⁡(K)O(K) work. Since Tmax=O⁡(B​Nmax2/log⁡(1+ε))T_{\max}=O(BN_{\max}^{2}/\log(1+\varepsilon)) and |𝒫|=L⁡(L−1)|\mathcal{P}|=L(L-1) is fixed, the per-grid-point cost is polynomial in KK, NmaxN_{\max}, and 1/ε1/\varepsilon. The grid 𝒢ε\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon} contains O​(Λ/log⁡(1+ε))|𝒫|O(\Lambda/\log(1+\varepsilon))^{|\mathcal{P}|} points, which is also polynomial in NmaxN_{\max} and 1/ε1/\varepsilon for fixed LL. Since Nmax=O⁡(log⁡(1/αmin))N_{\max}=O(\log(1/\alpha_{\min})) by Lemma 12, the overall runtime is polynomial in KK, log⁡(1/αmin)\log(1/\alpha_{\min}), and 1/ε1/\varepsilon.

Multiplicative cost bound. It remains to prove C⁡(r^)≤(1+ε)​OPT¯​(α)C(\widehat{r})\leq(1+\varepsilon)\,\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha) for sufficiently small αmin\alpha_{\min}. Let r⋆r^{\star} denote an optimal surrogate design with cost C​(r⋆)=OPT¯​(α)C(r^{\star})=\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha). The proof proceeds by constructing an explicit feasible solution for the DP at some grid point s¯∈𝒢ε|𝒫|\bar{s}\in\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon}^{|\mathcal{P}|} whose cost we can control, then arguing that the DP output is at least as cheap as this constructed solution. To absorb the two sources of approximation error that the algorithm introduces (grid discretization and weight rounding), we first augment r⋆r^{\star} with additional queries to every model, creating a (1+ε)2(1+\varepsilon)^{2} margin of slack in the surrogate constraints.

Constructing a near-feasible augmented design. For each ordered pair p=(y,y′)∈𝒫p=(y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{P}, select any minimizer

sp⋆∈arg⁡mins∈[0,1]​P¯y,y′​(r⋆,s),s_{p}^{\star}\in\arg\min_{s\in[0,1]}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star};s),

which exists because [0,1][0,1] is compact and s↦P¯y,y′​(r⋆,s)s\mapsto\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star};s) is continuous. Setting s⋆:=(sp⋆)p∈𝒫∈[0,1]|𝒫|s^{\star}:=(s_{p}^{\star})_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\in[0,1]^{|\mathcal{P}|} and applying Proposition 2 gives

P¯e​(y,r⋆,s⋆)=∑y′≠yP¯y,y′​(r⋆,s(y,y′)⋆)=∑y′≠ymins∈[0,1]⁡P¯y,y′​(r⋆,s)=P¯e​(y,r⋆)≤αy\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star};s^{\star})=\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star};s^{\star}_{(y,y^{\prime})})=\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\min_{s\in[0,1]}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star};s)=\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star})\leq\alpha_{y}

for every y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y}, so the pair (r⋆,s⋆)(r^{\star},s^{\star}) is feasible for the joint formulation (11).

We now verify that every component of s⋆s^{\star} lies in the interior interval [δ,1−δ][\delta,1-\delta]. Since r⋆r^{\star} is surrogate-feasible, Theorem 2 gives

Pe​(y,r⋆)≤P¯e​(y,r⋆)≤αy∀y∈𝒴,P_{e}(y;r^{\star})\leq\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star})\leq\alpha_{y}\qquad\forall\,y\in\mathcal{Y},

so r⋆r^{\star} is also feasible for the original robust problem (4). The assumption αmin≤ε0\alpha_{\min}\leq\varepsilon_{0} then places us in the regime of Lemma 10, which yields ny,y′​(r⋆)≥n0n_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\geq n_{0} for all y≠y′y\neq y^{\prime}. By construction n0≥ncenn_{0}\geq n_{\mathrm{cen}}, so ny,y′​(r⋆)≥ncenn_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star})\geq n_{\mathrm{cen}} and Lemma 5 gives sp⋆∈[δ,1−δ]s^{\star}_{p}\in[\delta,1-\delta] for every p∈𝒫p\in\mathcal{P}.

Define k⁡(ε):=⌈2​log⁡(1+ε)/(−log⁡ϑ)⌉k(\varepsilon):=\lceil 2\log(1+\varepsilon)/(-\log\vartheta)\rceil and the augmented design r~:=r⋆+k⁡(ε)​ 1\widetilde{r}:=r^{\star}+k(\varepsilon)\,\mathbf{1}, where 𝟏=(1,…,1)∈ℤ≥0K\mathbf{1}=(1,\ldots,1)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{K}. Because sp⋆∈[δ,1−δ]s^{\star}_{p}\in[\delta,1-\delta] for every pp, the definition of ϑ\vartheta in Lemma 9 gives ∏m=1KMm(y,y′)​(sp⋆)≤ϑ\prod_{m=1}^{K}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\leq\vartheta for every ordered pair p=(y,y′)p=(y,y^{\prime}). For any such pair, the pairwise Chernoff bound of the augmented design evaluated at sp⋆s_{p}^{\star} satisfies

P¯y,y′​(r~,sp⋆)\displaystyle\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(\widetilde{r};s^{\star}_{p}\big) =(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))sp⋆​∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(sp⋆))rm⋆+k⁡(ε)\displaystyle=\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s^{\star}_{p}}\prod_{m=1}^{K}\left(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\right)^{r^{\star}_{m}+k(\varepsilon)}
=(π⁡(y′)π⁡(y))sp⋆​∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(sp⋆))rm⋆⋅∏m=1K(Mm(y,y′)​(sp⋆))k⁡(ε)\displaystyle=\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime})}{\pi(y)}\right)^{s^{\star}_{p}}\prod_{m=1}^{K}\left(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\right)^{r^{\star}_{m}}\cdot\prod_{m=1}^{K}\left(M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\right)^{k(\varepsilon)}
=P¯y,y′​(r⋆,sp⋆)⋅(∏m=1KMm(y,y′)​(sp⋆))k⁡(ε)\displaystyle=\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(r^{\star};s^{\star}_{p}\big)\cdot\left(\prod_{m=1}^{K}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\right)^{k(\varepsilon)}
≤P¯y,y′​(r⋆,sp⋆)​ϑk⁡(ε),\displaystyle\leq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(r^{\star};s^{\star}_{p}\big)\,\vartheta^{k(\varepsilon)}, (30)

where the final inequality uses ∏m=1KMm(y,y′)​(sp⋆)≤ϑ\prod_{m=1}^{K}M_{m}^{(y,y^{\prime})}(s^{\star}_{p})\leq\vartheta. The definition of k⁡(ε)k(\varepsilon) guarantees that k⁡(ε)≥2​log⁡(1+ε)/(−log⁡ϑ)k(\varepsilon)\geq 2\log(1+\varepsilon)/(-\log\vartheta), which implies

ϑk⁡(ε)=ek⁡(ε)​log⁡ϑ≤e−2​log⁡(1+ε)=1(1+ε)2.\vartheta^{k(\varepsilon)}=e^{\,k(\varepsilon)\log\vartheta}\leq e^{\,-2\log(1+\varepsilon)}=\frac{1}{(1+\varepsilon)^{2}}.

Substituting this into (30) gives P¯y,y′​(r~,sp⋆)≤P¯y,y′​(r⋆,sp⋆)/(1+ε)2\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(\widetilde{r};s^{\star}_{p})\leq\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(r^{\star};s^{\star}_{p})/(1+\varepsilon)^{2}. Summing over y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y then yields

P¯e​(y,r~,s⋆)=∑y′≠yP¯y,y′​(r~,s(y,y′)⋆)≤1(1+ε)2​∑y′≠yP¯y,y′​(r⋆,s(y,y′)⋆)=P¯e​(y,r⋆,s⋆)(1+ε)2≤αy(1+ε)2\overline{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{r};s^{\star})=\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(\widetilde{r};s^{\star}_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big)\leq\frac{1}{(1+\varepsilon)^{2}}\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(r^{\star};s^{\star}_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big)=\frac{\overline{P}_{e}(y;r^{\star};s^{\star})}{(1+\varepsilon)^{2}}\leq\frac{\alpha_{y}}{(1+\varepsilon)^{2}} (31)

for every y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y}. The augmented design therefore satisfies the surrogate constraints with a quadratic margin of (1+ε)2(1+\varepsilon)^{2}. This margin will absorb the two approximation losses that follow.

We also verify that N⁡(r~)≤NmaxN(\widetilde{r})\leq N_{\max}. Lemma 12 gives C⁡(r⋆)≤nunif​cΣC(r^{\star})\leq n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma}, and since C⁡(r⋆)=∑mcm​rm⋆≥cmin​∑mrm⋆=cmin​N​(r⋆)C(r^{\star})=\sum_{m}c_{m}r_{m}^{\star}\geq c_{\min}\sum_{m}r_{m}^{\star}=c_{\min}\,N(r^{\star}), we obtain N⁡(r⋆)≤nunif​cΣ/cminN(r^{\star})\leq n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma}/c_{\min}. Because log⁡(1+ε)≤log⁡2\log(1+\varepsilon)\leq\log 2 for ε∈(0,1]\varepsilon\in(0,1], the ceiling definition gives k⁡(ε)≤kmaxk(\varepsilon)\leq k_{\max}, so

N⁡(r~)=N⁡(r⋆)+k⁡(ε)​K≤nunif​cΣcmin+kmax​K=Nmax.N(\widetilde{r})=N(r^{\star})+k(\varepsilon)\,K\leq\frac{n_{\mathrm{unif}}\,c_{\Sigma}}{c_{\min}}+k_{\max}\,K=N_{\max}.

This confirms that Lemmas 13 and 14 apply to r~\widetilde{r}.

Snapping s⋆s^{\star} to the grid. The grid 𝒢ε\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon} in Algorithm 4.3 has mesh h=log⁡(1+ε)/Λh=\log(1+\varepsilon)/\Lambda. There exists a grid point s¯∈𝒢ε|𝒫|\bar{s}\in\mathcal{G}_{\varepsilon}^{|\mathcal{P}|} such that |sp⋆−s¯p|≤h|s^{\star}_{p}-\bar{s}_{p}|\leq h for every p∈𝒫p\in\mathcal{P}. Applying Lemma 13 to each pair (y,y′)(y,y^{\prime}) gives

=(1+ε)​P¯y,y′​(r~,s(y,y′)⋆),\displaystyle=(1+\varepsilon)\,\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}(\widetilde{r};s^{\star}_{(y,y^{\prime})}),

where the final equality uses Λ​h=log⁡(1+ε)\Lambda\,h=\log(1+\varepsilon). Summing over y′≠yy^{\prime}\neq y and applying (31) gives

P¯e​(y,r~,s¯)=∑y′≠yP¯y,y′​(r~,s¯(y,y′))≤(1+ε)​∑y′≠yP¯y,y′​(r~,s(y,y′)⋆)=(1+ε)​P¯e​(y,r~,s⋆)≤αy1+ε\overline{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{r};\bar{s})=\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(\widetilde{r};\bar{s}_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big)\leq(1+\varepsilon)\sum_{y^{\prime}\neq y}\overline{P}_{y,y^{\prime}}\!\big(\widetilde{r};s^{\star}_{(y,y^{\prime})}\big)=(1+\varepsilon)\,\overline{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{r};s^{\star})\leq\frac{\alpha_{y}}{1+\varepsilon} (32)

for every y∈𝒴y\in\mathcal{Y}. One of the two factors of (1+ε)(1+\varepsilon) in the margin has now been consumed.

Rounding weights to DP states. Let t:=W~​(r~,s¯)t:=\widetilde{W}(\widetilde{r};\bar{s}) denote the rounded weight vector computed by Algorithm 4.3 at grid point s¯\bar{s}. By Lemma 14, rounding each weight wm,p​(s¯p)w_{m,p}(\bar{s}_{p}) down to its nearest multiple of Δ=log⁡(1+ε)/Nmax\Delta=\log(1+\varepsilon)/N_{\max} introduces a per-model error of at most Δ\Delta, and summing over the N⁡(r~)≤NmaxN(\widetilde{r})\leq N_{\max} queries yields a total rounding gap of at most Nmax⋅Δ=log⁡(1+ε)N_{\max}\cdot\Delta=\log(1+\varepsilon) in each coordinate. Exponentiating, this gives

P^e​(y,t,s¯)≤exp⁡(log⁡(1+ε))​P¯e​(y,r~,s¯)=(1+ε)​P¯e​(y,r~,s¯).\widehat{P}_{e}(y;t;\bar{s})\leq\exp\!\big(\log(1+\varepsilon)\big)\,\overline{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{r};\bar{s})=(1+\varepsilon)\,\overline{P}_{e}(y;\widetilde{r};\bar{s}).

Combining with (32) yields

P^e​(y,t,s¯)≤(1+ε)⋅αy1+ε=αy,∀y∈𝒴.\widehat{P}_{e}(y;t;\bar{s})\leq(1+\varepsilon)\cdot\frac{\alpha_{y}}{1+\varepsilon}=\alpha_{y},\qquad\forall\,y\in\mathcal{Y}.

The second and final factor of (1+ε)(1+\varepsilon) in the margin has been consumed, and r~\widetilde{r} is feasible for the DP feasibility condition at the grid point s¯\bar{s}.

Comparing costs. Because r~\widetilde{r} satisfies the DP feasibility condition at s¯\bar{s}, Proposition 4 gives C⁡(r†​(s¯))≤C⁡(r~)C(r^{\dagger}(\bar{s}))\leq C(\widetilde{r}). Algorithm 4.3 outputs the cheapest design across all grid points, so

C⁡(r^)≤C⁡(r†​(s¯))≤C⁡(r~)=C⁡(r⋆)+k⁡(ε)​cΣ=OPT¯​(α)+k⁡(ε)​cΣ.C(\widehat{r})\leq C(r^{\dagger}(\bar{s}))\leq C(\widetilde{r})=C(r^{\star})+k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}=\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)+k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}. (33)

Converting the additive bound to a multiplicative bound. It remains to show that k⁡(ε)​cΣ≤ε​OPT¯​(α)k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}\leq\varepsilon\,\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha) for sufficiently small αmin\alpha_{\min}. Define α0​(ε):=(L−1)​πminπmax​exp⁡(−B​k​(ε)​cΣε​cmin)\alpha_{0}(\varepsilon):=\frac{(L-1)\pi_{\min}}{\pi_{\max}}\exp\!\big(-\frac{B\,k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}}{\varepsilon\,c_{\min}}\big) and assume αmin≤α0​(ε)\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_{0}(\varepsilon). Taking logarithms of both sides of αmin≤α0​(ε)\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_{0}(\varepsilon) gives

which rearranges to

B​k​(ε)​cΣε​cmin≤log⁡((L−1)​πminπmax​αmin).\frac{B\,k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}}{\varepsilon\,c_{\min}}\leq\log\!\Big(\frac{(L-1)\,\pi_{\min}}{\pi_{\max}\,\alpha_{\min}}\Big). (34)

Applying Lemma 16 and using (34) yields

OPT¯​(α)≥cminB​log⁡((L−1)​πminπmax​αmin)≥cminB⋅B​k​(ε)​cΣε​cmin=k⁡(ε)​cΣε.\overline{\mathrm{OPT}}(\alpha)\;\geq\;\frac{c_{\min}}{B}\,\log\!\Big(\frac{(L-1)\,\pi_{\min}}{\pi_{\max}\,\alpha_{\min}}\Big)\;\geq\;\frac{c_{\min}}{B}\cdot\frac{B\,k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}}{\varepsilon\,c_{\min}}\;=\;\frac{k(\varepsilon)\,c_{\Sigma}}{\varepsilon}.
